title: Hold a post-launch review
summary: A few weeks after launch, step back as a team: did the product achieve what you hoped, what did you learn, and what will you do differently next time?

beginner: Book the review two to six weeks after launch, once there is real data.
Gather the results against your hypothesis and success metrics.
Ask everyone what went well, what did not and what surprised them.
Focus on the process and decisions, never on blaming people.
Agree three or four actions with owners.
Share a short summary with stakeholders.
intermediate: Review outcomes against the hypothesis and metrics.
Review delivery: plan versus actual, and why.
experienced: Compare the outcome with the original business case and be honest about the gap.
Look for patterns across several launches.
Feed lessons into planning and estimation practices.
Share learning across teams, including failures.

toolExamples.confluence: Use a retrospective template and link it to the product brief.
toolExamples.miro: Run the review on a board with sections for results, delivery and actions.
toolExamples.google-docs: Write a one-page summary for stakeholders.

pitfalls: Holding it too early, before there is data

sources.title: Postmortem culture: learning from failure (Google SRE book)
